methodology.startup: Successful non-warmup observations only; separate fresh browser contexts with alternating framework order
methodology.bootstrapPrimary: Independent sample percentile bootstrap for median(J) - median(W), in ms
methodology.bootstrapSensitivity: Complete same-source, same-round pairs resampled together; statistic remains median(J) - median(W)
methodology.memory: Successful rounds only; medians across rounds per stage/cycle; CDP after forced GC; MiB = 1048576 bytes
methodology.memoryDelta: Median of per-round stage heap minus that same round core heap

stability.expected: A visible child handles a click and invokes mount/unmount lifecycle hooks in order.
Props reach the child and a targeted host ping receives exactly one child pong.
Child global writes do not mutate the host global with the same name.
Child CSS applies inside the child and cannot recolor a matching host element.
Two concurrent apps render and keep click state and targeted bus messages independent.
Explicit destroy removes the child; a new instance resets state and has one bus subscription.
Switching away from a kept-alive app and back preserves its DOM state without remount.
Child pushState updates its own route while the host URL stays unchanged.
Child pushState updates its route and the named host query parameter without changing host pathname.
The destroy Promise completes only after the 80 ms async unmount hook and afterUnmount event.
Destroy during resource loading leaves no late mounted child or uncaught error after work settles.
Two overlapping starts for one name leave at most one live DOM; the latest request owns its container.
An executed preload can be activated, rendered in the requested container and interacted with.
Dynamically appended script and stylesheet finish loading and survive a kept-alive switch.
A script HTTP 404 is observable; after explicit cleanup, the same name starts successfully with a valid URL.
With fiber scheduling enabled, rendering, interaction and destroy still complete correctly.
